topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: It sets out the lecture's learning objectives, reviews the multistep progression model, and introduces the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Growth Factor Independence and Proliferative Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt/beta-catenin, and downstream cascades drive autonomous proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Malignancies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how blocks to normal cellular differentiation contribute to tumorigenesis in both hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how p53 disruption and the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins like Bax and BCL2 prevent programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Cellular Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how telomere shortening triggers senescence and how telomerase reactivation bypasses the Hayflick limit to allow indefinite replication.

topics.label: Deregulated Cancer Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex hallmarks to explain aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring, and the role of oncometabolites in tumor biology.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the angiogenic switch and the mechanisms by which tumors induce vascularization to support nutrient and oxygen perfusion.

topics.label: Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the metastatic cascade, circulation dynamics, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and the clonal genetics underlying tumor dissemination.

topics.label: Conclusion and Final Summary
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing framing by summarizing the cancer hallmarks paradigm, referencing recent literature, and inviting final questions.
